context.title: Costs per order

prompt: What contribution does the pizzeria make on an average order?
shortcut: Turn the percentage into dollars first ($4.20), then subtract all four costs: 28 − 17.70.

context.text: A juice bottling line fills 12,000 bottles per shift. Each shift costs $1,800 in labour and $600 in energy, and the bottle, cap and juice cost $0.18 per bottle.

prompt: What is the total cost per bottle?
shortcut: 2,400 ÷ 12,000 = 0.2; then add the per-bottle materials.

context.text: A podcast app has 3.2 million monthly users. 15% of them pay a $10 monthly subscription. The rest use the free tier, which earns $0.40 per user per month from advertising.

prompt: What is the app's average monthly revenue per user?
shortcut: Work per user, not in totals: weight each revenue by its share of users. The 3.2 million cancels out.

context.text: A meal-kit company makes a margin of $12 a month on each subscriber. Subscribers stay for 9 months on average, and winning each one costs $70 in marketing.

prompt: What profit does the company make over the lifetime of an average subscriber, after the marketing cost?
shortcut: Lifetime value minus acquisition cost: 108 − 70.

context.text: A supermarket sells its own-brand basmati rice in four pack sizes.

prompt: Which pack has the lowest price per kilogram?
options: 1 kg pack
2.5 kg pack
5 kg pack
10 kg pack

context.text: A taxi driver earns $0.90 for every kilometre driven with a passenger. He drives 220 km a day, 30% of it without a passenger. Fuel and wear cost $0.25 for every kilometre driven.

prompt: What is the driver's daily profit?
shortcut: Revenue counts only paid kilometres, costs count all of them. Charging costs on paid kilometres only gives $100.10, the trap.

context.text: An e-scooter operator is reviewing the economics of a single scooter.

items: Rides per scooter per day: 6
Average fare per ride, including the unlock fee: $3.50
Charging and repairs: 25% of fare revenue
City licence fee: $0.30 per ride
Scooter purchase price: $600, lasting 200 days of service

prompt: What is the daily profit per scooter after spreading its purchase price over its life?
solution: Licence fees: 6 × $0.30 = $1.80; scooter cost per day: $600 ÷ 200 = $3.00
shortcut: Per day: 15.75 kept, less 1.80 and 3.00. Leaving out the scooter itself gives $13.95, the trap.

context.text: A recruitment agency charges employers 18% of a placed candidate's first-year salary. Its average placement has a salary of $65,000. Each recruiter costs $90,000 a year in pay, carries $25,000 a year of office overheads and makes 14 placements a year.

prompt: Approximately how much profit does the agency make per placement?
shortcut: A recruiter's fees are 14 × 11.7k ≈ 164k a year against 115k of cost: about 49k ÷ 14 ≈ 3.5k each.

context.text: A 120-room city hotel runs at 75% occupancy with an average daily room rate of $160. Each occupied room also brings in $35 a night from breakfast, parking and the bar.

prompt: What is the hotel's total revenue per available room per night?
shortcut: Per available room = occupancy × revenue per occupied room; the 120 rooms do not matter.

context.text: An artisan bakery bakes 2,000 loaves a day. Flour, yeast and packaging cost $0.60 per loaf, and the bakery's daily fixed costs are $1,400. It plans to raise output to 2,800 loaves a day with no change in fixed costs.

prompt: By how much will the cost per loaf fall?
shortcut: Only the fixed share changes: 1,400 ÷ 2,000 = 0.70 against 1,400 ÷ 2,800 = 0.50.

context.text: A print shop's large-format press is fully booked, so the manager wants to favour the jobs that earn the most per hour of press time.

options: Brochures
Posters

shortcut: When capacity is the constraint, rank by contribution per unit of the scarce resource; brochures earn the most per job but the least per hour.

context.text: A fitness app spent $1.2m on a marketing campaign that produced 300,000 downloads. 40% of those who downloaded became active users, and 25% of active users bought a subscription at $8 a month.

prompt: What was the campaign's marketing cost per subscriber won?
shortcut: Only 10% of downloads subscribe (0.4 × 0.25), so the cost per subscriber is ten times the $4 per download.

context.text: An online grocer is reviewing the economics of a typical home-delivery order.

items: Average basket: $72, with a gross margin of 28% on the groceries
Delivery fee: $4, paid on 60% of orders; members pay nothing for delivery
Picking and packing: $6 per order
Van and driver: $9 per order

prompt: What is the grocer's contribution per order?
shortcut: Average the delivery fee over all orders ($2.40); charging it on every order gives $9.16 and dropping it gives $5.16.

context.text: A parcel firm pays its drivers $22 an hour plus $1.50 per delivery, and earns $6.50 in fees per delivery. Vans cost $0.40 per km to run. Each delivery adds 3 km, and drivers also cover 6 km every hour moving between zones, however many deliveries they make.

prompt: Roughly how many deliveries an hour must a driver make for the fees to cover driver pay and van costs?
options: 4.4 deliveries
5.8 deliveries
6.4 deliveries
7.2 deliveries
shortcut: Split costs into per-hour and per-delivery, then divide one by the margin on the other. Ignoring the van gives 22 ÷ 5 = 4.4.

context.text: A project-management software firm charges $50 per customer per month, at a gross margin of 80%. Each month 4% of customers cancel, and it costs $600 to win a new customer. Assume a customer's expected lifetime in months is 1 divided by the monthly cancellation rate.

prompt: Approximately what is the ratio of a customer's lifetime gross margin to the cost of winning them?
shortcut: Monthly margin $40 ÷ 4% churn = $1,000. Using revenue rather than margin ($1,250) gives 2.1×, the trap.

context.text: An airline is reviewing one daily route flown with a 180-seat aircraft. Fuel, crew and airport charges come to $28,000 per flight.

prompt: Approximately what profit does the airline make per flight?
shortcut: Apply each cabin's own load factor. Using 90% for both gives $8,900, and full planes give $13,000.

context.text: A café sells 400 coffees a day at $4.50. Milk and beans cost $0.90 per coffee, and each disposable cup costs $0.20. The owner plans to switch to compostable cups at $0.05 each, but customers find them flimsy, and she expects to sell 10% fewer coffees as a result.

prompt: How will the switch change the café's daily contribution from coffee?
shortcut: Lost sales cost 40 × $3.40 = $136; the cheaper cups save 360 × $0.15 = $54; net −$82.

shortcut: Lease income is $1,020 a year, maintenance takes $150, so $870 × 15 = $13,050, less $10,200 of one-off costs.

context.text: Fornello is a chain of about 70 pizza restaurants. Its margins have been shrinking over the past year as the price of locally made mozzarella keeps going up. The purchasing manager proposes buying imported mozzarella instead for the chain's best-selling Margherita pizza.

Imported mozzarella costs $10 per kg for the first 150,000 kg bought in a year and $7 per kg after that
Dough, sauce and the other costs of making a Margherita come to $2.50 per pizza
Each Margherita uses 0.2 kg of mozzarella

Using imported mozzarella costs $110,000 more per year

Using imported mozzarella costs $280,000 more per year

The blended wax costs $5 per kg on the first 380,000 kg each year and $2 per kg beyond that

The blended wax would cost $450,000 more a year than soy wax
